title: Harmonic Autoscale Controller and Burst Fidelity Reporter
author: Aditi Rao
description: Context: Customers running Dedicated fleets observed oscillatory scale behaviour during intermittent multi-tenant microbursts and poor observability into burst fidelity (how closely a burst payload matched a capacity reservation). Motivation: Reduce oscillation while preserving rapid burst acceptance for short-lived spikes and provide actionable telemetry so SRE and capacity-planning teams can tune reserve and burst policies. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a new harmonic autoscale controller that uses a harmonic-mean based estimator over multiple utilization windows to bias scaling decisions toward preventing under-provisioning during bursts while damping noisy high-percentile samples. The controller exposes knobs: burst_window (seconds), smoothing_alpha (0..1), min_commit_reserve_pct, and scale_step_ceiling. 2) Adds a Burst Fidelity Reporter that aggregates per-tenant burst events and reports fidelity metrics: peak_to_average, burst_duration_ms, headroom_violation_count, accepted_vs_rejected_burst_ratio, and a histogram of instantaneous utilization during bursts. The reporter emits Prometheus-compatible metrics and an export for longer-term S3-backed rollups. 3) Adds a safety policy layer that prevents aggressive downscales for a configurable cooldown after any detected burst acceptance and ties decays to harmonic estimates rather than raw instantaneous utilization. Design notes: The harmonic estimator is deliberately conservative for tail events (H = n / sum(1/x_i)) — it reduces the influence of extreme high samples compared to arithmetic mean but still responds quickly when many samples are elevated. We combine multiple windows (short, medium, long) with weights to enable both quick reaction and stability. The Burst Fidelity Reporter uses lightweight sampling (1% by default) and event-aggregation to avoid adding CPU overhead to the serving path. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% of Dedicated pools) -> 25% -> 75% -> all, with a contingency to revert to arithmetic-based controller if tail latency regressions exceed 3x baseline for two consecutive 5-minute windows. Backwards compatibility: Controller honours existing per-tenant reservation and burst-credit configs; defaults keep behaviour unchanged until operators opt-in. Migration: includes a feature flag (harmonic_autoscale_enabled) and a Helm values toggle. Testing and validation: unit tests for estimator math and controller state transitions; integration tests running synthetic burst traces against a local cluster; k8s e2e manifest for controller and reporter. Observability and alerts: new SLO alarms for sustained headroom_violation_count > 5/min and a dashboard that surfaces accepted/rejected burst ratio per-tenant. Related: follows ENG-2419 (autoscaler stability initiative) and ENG-2543 (dedicated burst observability).

release_notes:
- Introduced Harmonic Autoscale Controller (opt-in via feature flag) to reduce oscillation while maintaining burst acceptance.
- Added Burst Fidelity Reporter: per-tenant burst metrics and histograms for capacity planning and SLO analysis.
- New tuning knobs: burst_window, smoothing_alpha, min_commit_reserve_pct, scale_step_ceiling.
- Safety policy prevents aggressive downscales shortly after burst acceptance.
